title: acer glabrum var. douglasii
intro: Acer glabrum var. douglasii, commonly known as the Douglas Maple or Rock Maple, is a deciduous shrub or small tree native to the western regions of North America. This plant is valued for its medicinal properties, which include reducing inflammation and pain, making it a potential remedy for conditions such as arthritis and muscle spasms. The bioactive constituents of Douglas Maple include salicin, a compound similar to aspirin, as well as other flavonoids and phenolic acids, which contribute to its therapeutic actions, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. Additionally, Douglas Maple has been traditionally used to treat various ailments, including fever, rheumatism, and skin conditions, due to its ability to stimulate the immune system and promote wound healing.
